title: Biological Laboratory Technology
source_note: Grounded in standard NUC-aligned biological laboratory technology curricula: microscopy, specimen preparation and staining, sterilization and aseptic technique, culture media, and biosafety practices typical of a 200-level Science Laboratory Technology programme.

questions.question: In a compound light microscope, which part is primarily responsible for the initial magnification of the specimen image, closest to the specimen?
options: The objective lens
The ocular (eyepiece) lens
The condenser
The iris diaphragm
questions.correct_answer: The objective lens
questions.explanation: The objective lens, positioned close to the specimen, produces the first magnified real image, which is then further magnified by the eyepiece.

questions.question: If a microscope's eyepiece has a magnification of 10x and the objective lens in use is 40x, what is the total magnification of the specimen?
options: 4x
questions.explanation: Total magnification = eyepiece magnification x objective magnification = 10 x 40 = 400x.

questions.question: What is the function of the condenser in a compound light microscope?
options: To focus and concentrate light from the illumination source onto the specimen
To magnify the final image seen by the eye
To hold the specimen slide in place
To adjust the coarse focus of the image
questions.correct_answer: To focus and concentrate light from the illumination source onto the specimen
questions.explanation: The condenser lens system gathers and focuses light onto the specimen plane, improving illumination and resolution of the viewed image.

questions.question: Immersion oil is used with the 100x (oil immersion) objective lens primarily to:
options: Increase the resolving power by reducing refraction of light as it passes from the slide to the objective lens
Clean the lens after use
Reduce the total magnification of the image
Prevent the specimen from drying out
questions.correct_answer: Increase the resolving power by reducing refraction of light as it passes from the slide to the objective lens
questions.explanation: Immersion oil has a refractive index close to that of glass, minimizing light refraction/scattering between the slide and lens, which improves resolution at high magnification.

questions.question: Why should the coarse focus adjustment knob never be used when viewing a specimen under the high-power (40x or 100x) objective lens?
options: It can cause the objective lens to crash into and damage the slide due to the very small working distance at high magnification
It only works with the low-power objective and has no physical effect at high power
It changes the colour of the specimen
It automatically switches off the light source
questions.correct_answer: It can cause the objective lens to crash into and damage the slide due to the very small working distance at high magnification
questions.explanation: At high magnification the working distance between lens and slide is extremely small, so using coarse focus risks the lens hitting and breaking the slide or damaging the lens.

questions.question: What is the correct first step before storing a compound microscope after use?
options: Clean the lenses with lens paper, remove the slide, rotate to the lowest power objective, and cover the microscope
Leave the slide in place for the next user
Store it with the highest power objective in position and immersion oil left on the lens
Disassemble the eyepiece completely
questions.correct_answer: Clean the lenses with lens paper, remove the slide, rotate to the lowest power objective, and cover the microscope
questions.explanation: Proper microscope care includes cleaning lenses (especially removing immersion oil), removing slides, returning to low power, and covering the instrument to protect it from dust.

questions.question: The Gram stain technique classifies bacteria into two broad groups based primarily on differences in:
options: Cell wall structure and peptidoglycan content
Cell shape only (rod versus sphere)
Motility of the organism
The colour of the growth medium
questions.correct_answer: Cell wall structure and peptidoglycan content
questions.explanation: Gram-positive bacteria have a thick peptidoglycan layer that retains crystal violet stain, while Gram-negative bacteria have a thin peptidoglycan layer and outer membrane that does not retain it, so they take up the counterstain instead.

questions.question: In the Gram staining procedure, what is the correct order of reagents applied to a heat-fixed smear?
options: Crystal violet, iodine (mordant), decolorizer (alcohol/acetone), safranin (counterstain)
Safranin, iodine, crystal violet, decolorizer
Decolorizer, crystal violet, safranin, iodine
Iodine, safranin, decolorizer, crystal violet
questions.correct_answer: Crystal violet, iodine (mordant), decolorizer (alcohol/acetone), safranin (counterstain)
questions.explanation: The standard Gram stain sequence is: primary stain (crystal violet), mordant (iodine) to fix the stain, decolorization, then counterstain (safranin) to colour Gram-negative cells pink.

questions.question: After Gram staining, Gram-positive bacteria appear which colour under the microscope?
options: Purple/violet
Pink/red
Green
Yellow
questions.correct_answer: Purple/violet
questions.explanation: Gram-positive bacteria retain the crystal violet-iodine complex due to their thick peptidoglycan wall, appearing purple; Gram-negative bacteria lose this stain and appear pink from the safranin counterstain.

questions.question: What is the purpose of heat-fixing a bacterial smear on a glass slide before staining?
options: To kill the organisms and adhere them firmly to the slide so they are not washed off during staining
To increase the size of the bacterial cells
To change the bacteria's Gram reaction
To colour the bacteria without needing a stain
questions.correct_answer: To kill the organisms and adhere them firmly to the slide so they are not washed off during staining
questions.explanation: Heat fixation coagulates cellular proteins, killing the organism and firmly attaching it to the slide, preventing it from washing away during the multiple rinsing steps of staining.

questions.question: Which sterilization method uses saturated steam under pressure, typically at 121°C for 15 minutes, and is the most common method for sterilizing culture media and instruments?
options: Autoclaving
Pasteurization
Filtration through a 0.22 micron membrane
UV irradiation
questions.correct_answer: Autoclaving
questions.explanation: Autoclaving uses pressurized steam (commonly 121°C, 15 psi, 15 minutes) to achieve complete sterilization by killing all microorganisms including spores.

questions.question: Which sterilization method is most appropriate for heat-sensitive liquids, such as certain vitamin or antibiotic solutions, that would be destroyed by autoclaving?
options: Membrane (0.22 micron) filtration
Dry heat oven at 160°C
Autoclaving at 121°C
Flaming
questions.correct_answer: Membrane (0.22 micron) filtration
questions.explanation: Filter sterilization physically removes microorganisms from heat-labile liquids by passing them through a membrane with pores small enough (typically 0.22 micron) to retain bacteria, avoiding heat damage.

questions.question: Dry heat sterilization in a hot air oven, typically used for glassware, generally requires which conditions?
options: A higher temperature and longer exposure time than autoclaving, e.g. 160-180°C for 1-2 hours
The same temperature and time as autoclaving
A lower temperature than autoclaving because dry heat penetrates faster
No specific temperature control is needed
questions.correct_answer: A higher temperature and longer exposure time than autoclaving, e.g. 160-180°C for 1-2 hours
questions.explanation: Dry heat is less efficient at killing microorganisms than moist heat, so it requires higher temperatures and longer exposure times to achieve sterilization compared to autoclaving.

questions.question: What indicates that an autoclave cycle has achieved adequate sterilization conditions, beyond simply reaching temperature?
options: A biological or chemical indicator (e.g. autoclave tape or spore strip) confirms the required time-temperature-pressure combination was met
The autoclave door opens automatically
The steam turns a visible colour
The load feels warm to the touch immediately after the cycle
questions.correct_answer: A biological or chemical indicator (e.g. autoclave tape or spore strip) confirms the required time-temperature-pressure combination was met
questions.explanation: Chemical indicators (colour-change tape) and biological indicators (spore strips) verify that sterilizing conditions were actually achieved throughout the load, not just that the cycle ran.

questions.question: Aseptic technique in microbiology practice is best described as:
options: A set of practices used to prevent contamination of cultures, media, and personnel by unwanted microorganisms
A method for staining bacteria
A technique for measuring bacterial growth rate
A method of disposing of laboratory waste
questions.correct_answer: A set of practices used to prevent contamination of cultures, media, and personnel by unwanted microorganisms
questions.explanation: Aseptic technique encompasses procedures (flaming loops, working near a Bunsen flame, minimizing exposure time) that prevent introduction of contaminating organisms into a sterile culture or environment.

questions.question: Why is an inoculating loop flamed to red-hot before and after transferring a bacterial culture?
options: To sterilize the loop and prevent cross-contamination between cultures
To cool the loop down quickly
To change the colour of the bacteria
To increase the size of the inoculum transferred
questions.correct_answer: To sterilize the loop and prevent cross-contamination between cultures
questions.explanation: Flaming the loop until red-hot kills any organisms on its surface, preventing contamination of the new culture and cross-contamination between different samples.

questions.question: Nutrient agar is an example of which type of culture medium?
options: A general-purpose (basal) medium supporting growth of a wide range of non-fastidious organisms
A medium that only supports fungal growth
A liquid medium used exclusively for antibiotic testing
A medium that kills all bacteria on contact
questions.correct_answer: A general-purpose (basal) medium supporting growth of a wide range of non-fastidious organisms
questions.explanation: Nutrient agar is a simple, general-purpose solid medium containing basic nutrients that supports the growth of many common, non-fastidious bacteria without special enrichment.

questions.question: A selective culture medium is designed to:
options: Encourage the growth of certain organisms while inhibiting the growth of others
Support the growth of every organism equally
Prevent all microbial growth entirely
Only be used for viewing specimens under the microscope
questions.correct_answer: Encourage the growth of certain organisms while inhibiting the growth of others
questions.explanation: Selective media contain agents (e.g. antibiotics, dyes, high salt) that suppress unwanted organisms while allowing target organisms to grow, aiding isolation from mixed samples.

questions.question: A differential culture medium is used primarily to:
options: Distinguish between different types of organisms growing on the same plate based on visible characteristics such as colour change
Sterilize a sample before analysis
Increase the shelf-life of the medium indefinitely
Replace the need for a microscope entirely
questions.correct_answer: Distinguish between different types of organisms growing on the same plate based on visible characteristics such as colour change
questions.explanation: Differential media contain indicators that produce visibly distinct reactions (e.g. colour changes) for different organisms, allowing them to be distinguished on the same plate without separate tests.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the streak plate technique in microbiology?
options: To progressively dilute a bacterial sample across the surface of an agar plate to obtain isolated, single colonies
To measure the exact number of bacteria in a sample
To stain bacteria for viewing under oil immersion
To sterilize the agar plate before use
questions.correct_answer: To progressively dilute a bacterial sample across the surface of an agar plate to obtain isolated, single colonies
questions.explanation: The streak plate method spreads and dilutes a mixed sample across successive sections of the plate, ultimately separating cells so that isolated colonies (each derived from one cell) can grow.

questions.question: Why is it important to work near a lit Bunsen burner flame when performing microbiological transfers on an open bench?
options: The rising hot air current helps carry airborne contaminants away from the immediate work area
The flame sterilizes the entire room instantly
It provides the only source of light for the technician
It has no real protective function, only tradition
questions.correct_answer: The rising hot air current helps carry airborne contaminants away from the immediate work area
questions.explanation: The convection current created by the flame creates a localized updraft that helps keep settling dust and airborne microbes away from the open culture, supporting aseptic technique.

questions.question: In a haemocytometer (counting chamber) used for cell counting, what does the ruled grid on the chamber allow the technician to determine?
options: The number of cells per unit volume of a suspension
The exact species of cell present
The colour of the cell suspension
The pH of the cell suspension
questions.correct_answer: The number of cells per unit volume of a suspension
questions.explanation: The haemocytometer has a grid of known area and chamber depth, so counting cells within defined squares allows calculation of cell concentration (cells per mL) in the original suspension.

questions.question: Which fixative is commonly used to preserve biological tissue specimens for histological examination, maintaining cellular structure close to the living state?
options: 10% formalin (formaldehyde solution)
Concentrated hydrochloric acid
Distilled water
Sodium chloride crystals
questions.correct_answer: 10% formalin (formaldehyde solution)
questions.explanation: Formalin is a standard chemical fixative that cross-links proteins, preserving tissue structure and preventing autolysis and putrefaction, widely used in histology.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of fixing a biological specimen before microscopic examination or long-term storage?
options: To preserve the cellular and tissue structure and prevent decay caused by autolysis and microbial action
To increase the size of the specimen
To dissolve the specimen for easier viewing
To colour the specimen a permanent bright colour
questions.correct_answer: To preserve the cellular and tissue structure and prevent decay caused by autolysis and microbial action
questions.explanation: Fixation halts enzymatic (autolytic) breakdown and microbial decay, preserving the specimen's structural integrity for later study or storage.

questions.question: In dissection practicals, why must all sharp instruments (scalpels, scissors, pins) be handled and disposed of with particular care?
options: To prevent cuts, punctures, and potential exposure to biological material
Because they are the most expensive items in the laboratory
Because they must always be shared without cleaning between students
Because they cannot be sterilized
questions.correct_answer: To prevent cuts, punctures, and potential exposure to biological material
questions.explanation: Sharps pose both a physical injury risk and a biological exposure risk if contaminated, so careful handling, use of sharps containers, and proper disposal are essential lab safety practices.

questions.question: Biohazardous laboratory waste, such as used culture plates and contaminated swabs, should be:
options: Autoclaved or otherwise decontaminated before disposal, and kept separate from general waste
Thrown directly into the general household waste bin
Washed down the sink without treatment
Left on the open bench until the end of the week
questions.correct_answer: Autoclaved or otherwise decontaminated before disposal, and kept separate from general waste
questions.explanation: Biohazardous waste must be rendered non-infectious (commonly via autoclaving) and segregated from general waste to prevent exposure and environmental contamination.

questions.question: What PPE is the minimum standard requirement when handling microbial cultures in a teaching microbiology laboratory?
options: Laboratory coat, gloves, and eye protection as appropriate to the task
Casual clothing with no protective gear
Open sandals for comfort
Gloves only, with no other protective clothing
questions.correct_answer: Laboratory coat, gloves, and eye protection as appropriate to the task
questions.explanation: Standard biosafety practice requires a lab coat, gloves, and eye protection (where splash risk exists) to protect the technician's skin, clothing, and eyes from biological contamination.

questions.question: Why must hands be washed thoroughly with soap and water (not just sanitized) after removing gloves at the end of a microbiology practical?
options: Gloves can have microscopic tears or contamination can occur during removal, and handwashing physically removes residual organisms
It has no real benefit beyond habit
It replaces the need to wear gloves at all
It is only necessary once a week
questions.correct_answer: Gloves can have microscopic tears or contamination can occur during removal, and handwashing physically removes residual organisms
questions.explanation: Gloves reduce but do not eliminate contact risk; handwashing after glove removal provides an additional physical barrier against residual contamination transferred during doffing.

questions.question: In serial dilution technique, if 1 mL of bacterial culture is added to 9 mL of sterile diluent, what dilution factor has been achieved?
options: 1 in 9
1 in 1
questions.explanation: The total volume after dilution is 1 mL + 9 mL = 10 mL, so the original sample is diluted 1 part in 10, giving a dilution factor of 10^-1.

questions.question: Why is serial dilution commonly performed before plating a bacterial sample for a viable count?
options: To reduce the bacterial concentration to a level where individual colonies can be distinguished and counted accurately on a plate
To kill all the bacteria before counting
To change the Gram reaction of the bacteria
To increase the total number of bacteria present
questions.correct_answer: To reduce the bacterial concentration to a level where individual colonies can be distinguished and counted accurately on a plate
questions.explanation: A concentrated sample plated directly would produce confluent, uncountable growth; serial dilution reduces the cell number so discrete, countable colonies form.

questions.question: What is the correct disposal method for a used glass Pasteur pipette or broken glass slide contaminated with biological material?
options: Dispose of it in a designated puncture-resistant sharps/glass waste container
Place it in the general paper recycling bin
Rinse it and reuse it immediately without sterilization
Leave it on the bench for the next student to dispose of
questions.correct_answer: Dispose of it in a designated puncture-resistant sharps/glass waste container
questions.explanation: Contaminated sharps and broken glass require disposal in dedicated puncture-resistant containers to prevent injury and control biohazard spread, separate from ordinary waste streams.
